title: Ravana's final battle
hook: a spear meant for Vibhishana, a brother who steps in front of it, and a chariot sent from heaven

segments.voice: Yesterday: Indrajit's death, at Nikumbhila, by Indra's own weapon, on a vow resting on Rama's goodness. Did you lean on someone you trust? Today, with his son gone, Ravana rides out for the last time. Day six hundred fifty-four.

Ravana has no one left to send. His brother Kumbhakarna is dead. His son Indrajit is dead. Most of his champions are gone. So he puts on his armor, mounts his great chariot, and rides out through the gates himself, with whatever army remains. The monkeys scatter before him. And in the enemy line he sees the brother who left him, Vibhishana. Ravana picks up a great spear, made to kill, and aims it at him.
screen: `NO ONE LEFT TO SEND.` → `RAVANA RIDES OUT.` → `A SPEAR AIMED AT VIBHISHANA.`

segments.voice: Lakshmana sees it, and he doesn't hesitate. He fires at Ravana again and again, drawing his attention away from Vibhishana. Remember Rama's vow on the beach: anyone who comes for refuge is safe. Lakshmana is keeping it with his own body. Ravana, furious, turns the spear on him. You saved him, he says, so take this instead. The spear strikes Lakshmana in the chest, and he falls. Rama pulls the spear out and breaks it, and then, Valmiki says, he sits by his brother and weeps. What would I do with victory, with Sita even, without Lakshmana? In Valmiki this is where the second herb flight comes. Sushena, the monkey physician, kneels and looks at Lakshmana's face. He isn't dead, he says; his face hasn't changed. He sends Hanuman to a mountain for herbs, and once more Hanuman comes back carrying a whole peak. Sushena crushes a herb and holds it to Lakshmana's nose, and he breathes it in and gets up. And now something else arrives from the sky. Rama has been fighting on foot this whole war, against a king in a chariot. The gods see it, and Indra sends his own chariot down to Rama, with his charioteer, Matali, holding the reins. Matali bows. This chariot is yours, he says. Rama walks around it with respect, and climbs aboard. For the first time, the two of them meet as equals: Ravana in his chariot, Rama in Indra's. The last battle can begin.
screen: `LAKSHMANA KEEPS RAMA'S VOW.` · `THE SPEAR STRIKES LAKSHMANA.` · `SUSHENA AND THE SECOND HERB.` · `INDRA'S CHARIOT AND MATALI.` · then, large: `FOR THE FIRST TIME, AS EQUALS.`

segments.voice: Sit, and let your breath slow. Think of a promise someone close to you made, one you could help them keep: a parent's promise, a friend's commitment, a team's word. Lakshmana kept his brother's vow without being asked. Picture one small way you could help. Hold it in mind. Breathe in, and feel steady. Breathe out, and feel ready. The bell holds the time.
Ravana's final battle. It begins with a spear aimed at Vibhishana, Lakshmana stepping into its path, Sushena's herb, and Indra's chariot sent down for Rama.
Your line: Ravana's final battle. Today, help someone keep a promise they made, without being asked. Day six hundred fifty-four.

howItsDone: Ramlila performances across North India build toward Ravana's final battle over many nights. Many follow Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, where the wounding of Lakshmana that audiences know best comes earlier, from Meghnad (Indrajit), and Sushena and Hanuman's mountain save him there.

original.note: Sanskrit Mātali: Indra's charioteer, who brings Indra's chariot to Rama for the final battle.

trapdoor: what you thought: Lakshmana was wounded by bad luck.
what it means: he drew a spear meant for Vibhishana onto himself, keeping Rama's vow of refuge.

what a scholar hears: in Valmiki, Sushena's herb saves Lakshmana from Ravana's spear; in Tulsidas, the famous wound comes from Meghnad's weapon instead, while Sushena and the mountain stay in the story.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 100–101 (Ravana's spear; Lakshmana falls; Sushena and the herbs)

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.
Ravana aiming the spear at Vibhishana first, and Lakshmana drawing it onto himself: confirm.

Rama's lament over Lakshmana (what use is victory without him): paraphrased; the famous verse about finding wives and kin in every land but not a brother is not used, as its location could not be confirmed.
The mountain Sushena names (often given as Mahodaya) is left unnamed; confirm.
Matali's words and Rama circling the chariot: paraphrased; confirm.

Audit (second sample): howItsDone and the trapdoor said Ramlila audiences and later tradition remember this spear wound as the saving of Lakshmana; in the Ramcharitmanas that most Ramlilas follow, the famous wound is Meghnad's weapon. Both now say so. Confirm the Ramcharitmanas details (Meghnad's shakti, Sushena fetched from Lanka, Hanuman's mountain).
